newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma declares 1996 income of $7,300.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma declares 1996 income of $7,300.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma, who is trying to clear up taxation chaos in Ukraine, has declared a 1996 income equivalent to just over $600 a month, Interfax-Ukraine news agency said on Saturday.
Kuchma sent a declaration to tax authorities saying he earned 13,355 hryvnias ($7,300 at current exchange rates) last year.
He also declared a dacha, or country home, worth $8,000 near his eastern industrial hometown of Dnipropetrovsk.
The average salary in Ukraine is about $80 to 90 per month.
"He (Kuchma) had no other income except that connected to carrying out his main duties. He has no incomes linked to business activities or from abroad," the agency said.
Kuchma has been pressing parliament for several months to pass new tax laws and improve collection to pave the way for a multi-billion dollar International Monetary Fund loan.
Many Ukrainians try to avoid paying taxes or attempt to hide at least part of their income and experts estimate that about 40 percent of the economy is underground.
